question: ADR-0002 Q7 cites commit #962 for the retention size cap, but that commit is unrelated (stats feature) - what is the real size-cap number and source?
verdict: citation is wrong and no such decision exists yet
answer: ADR-0002 Q7 and DECISIONS-r3.md Q7 cite '#962' as the source for a retention size cap. #962 is not a commit, it is issue #962: 'RFC: bound trigram/vocab growth for logs/JSONL' (tickets/map-I3.md:6, tickets/v2-issue-map.md:215). Its own status is 'not discussed (storage/index policy)' and ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md:56 lists it as needs-decision, no: 'How is trigram/vocabulary growth bounded for logs/JSONL content...'. tickets/v2-not-closed.md:18 and :31 list I962 among the 10 questions the v2 list says must still be decided. So #962 is about FTS5 vocabulary/trigram growth, not about an overall index/retention byte size cap, and it has never been decided - there is no number behind it anywhere in tickets/ or docs/. The only actual byte cap that exists anywhere in v1 is MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 4096, a per-chunk cap unrelated to retention (src/store.ts:153), introduced in commit 609a3a5a 'feat: JSON chunking, maxChunkBytes, and content-type routing' and hardened in 6f699fac 'fix(store): enforce MAX_CHUNK_BYTES in #chunkPlainText to prevent FTS5 DB bloat (#789)'. Neither commit mentions retention or eviction; MAX_CHUNK_BYTES only bounds a single chunk's size when splitting text, it does not bound total index size or trigger eviction. A separate ticket, #878 'chunkMarkdown oversized paragraphs' (tickets/map-I3.md:40), is also about the same per-chunk byte cap, not a retention cap. Conclusion: there is no real size-cap number. The ADR's citation points to the wrong issue entirely, and the right issue (#962) is still an open RFC with no number decided.

MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.INTRODUCED_BY: 609a3a5a 2026-03-03 'feat: JSON chunking, maxChunkBytes, and content-type routing'
MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.HARDENED_BY: 6f699fac 2026-06-13 'fix(store): enforce MAX_CHUNK_BYTES in #chunkPlainText to prevent FTS5 DB bloat (#789)'
MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.ORIGINAL_INTENT: Quote from 6f699fac body: 'plain-text content with few lines ... or a few very long lines could produce oversized chunks that bloated the FTS5 content DB and caused search timeouts.' Current value: src/store.ts:153 const MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 4096;
MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.REGRESSION_RISK: If v2 drops or changes MAX_CHUNK_BYTES enforcement in chunking paths without an equivalent cap, oversized chunks can again bloat the FTS5 DB and cause search timeouts (same failure mode as #789/#781).
MAX_CHUNK_BYTES.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: Preserve the 4096-byte per-chunk cap across all chunking paths (markdown, plain text, JSON) if reused in v2; this is NOT a substitute for a retention/eviction size cap and must not be presented as one.

issue_962.STATUS: needs-decision, not discussed. tickets/map-I3.md:6, tickets/v2-issue-map.md:215, ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md:56, v2-not-closed.md:18/:31
issue_962.TOPIC: trigram/vocabulary growth bound for logs/JSONL content, not a retention or total-index size cap

docGapDetail: ADR-0002 (section with Q7) and docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md:13 cite '#962' as the source for the retention size cap decision. Neither document states the actual numeric cap, and #962 itself (per tickets/v2-issue-map.md and ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md) is a different, undecided RFC about vocabulary growth, not a size cap.
recommendedAnswer: Fix the citation in ADR-0002 Q7 and DECISIONS-r3.md Q7: remove the '#962' citation (wrong topic) and either (a) pick a real numeric retention/index size cap (e.g. total index bytes or chunk-count ceiling) as a new owner decision, since no existing commit or issue defines one, or (b) if MAX_CHUNK_BYTES=4096 per-chunk is meant to stand in for 'bounded growth', say so explicitly and acknowledge it does not cap total index size.

findings.claim: Q7: retention = age + live owner PID + a size cap (#962).
findings.evidence: #962 is issue 'RFC: bound trigram/vocab growth for logs/JSONL' (tickets/v2-issue-map.md:215), status 'not discussed', listed as needs-decision/no in ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md:56 and still open in tickets/v2-not-closed.md:18,31. No commit numbered 962 exists in git log; the actual commit at position 962 in the ancestry chain (e42ea655) is an unrelated merge. No numeric size cap is defined anywhere in tickets/ or src/.
findings.fix: Replace the #962 citation with either a new owner-decided numeric size cap, or explicitly mark Q7's size-cap clause as unresolved pending #962's RFC outcome.
